text: The EDA pointed at real signals. Now they become an actual training table -- one row per account per monthly snapshot, with a correct 90-day-forward label.
Demographic features -- tenure, SeatCount, PlanTier, MonthlyRevenue -- are re-derived fresh for each snapshot's own OBSERVATION_DATE. Nothing borrows a date that doesn't belong to that row.

The behavioral features: logins_last_30d and days_since_last_login. Each account gets one reference point -- its ChurnDate if it churned, otherwise today -- and the login window counts back from there.
Open support tickets in the last 90 days and invoice lateness over the last 180 roll up against that same reference point, for consistency across the whole feature set.
One complete, labeled feature table comes out the other side, saved to parquet. Next: training the baseline and the gradient-boosted model on it.
